message.content:
This is a CBP ruling about an aluminum laminate film from a company in Düren, Germany (likely Renolit). The product is a composite of aluminum foil, PET film and protective film. Heading 7607 covers aluminum foil, whether or not printed or backed with paper, paperboard, plastics or similar backing materials, with a thickness not exceeding 0.2 mm excluding backing. Here the aluminum is 0.08 mm thick, and the backing is PET.

Subheading 7607.19 covers foil that is not backed, and 7607.20 covers foil that is backed. Backed foil goes to 7607.20.50 ("Other") or 7607.20.10 (insulating foil?). In the HTSUS, 7607.20.10 is "Backed with paper, paperboard, plastics or similar backing materials: Not over 0.15 mm thick" and 7607.20.50 is "Other." The statistical suffixes under 7607.20.10 are 7607.20.1000 and 7607.20.5000. Under 7607.20.50 the suffixes are 7607.20.5010 (Aluminum foil, backed, over 0.15 mm?), and I am not certain of the exact statistical breakdown.

The tariff text says "Backed: Of a thickness (excluding any backing) not exceeding 0.15 mm" and falls under 7607.20.10, which covers thickness not exceeding 0.15 mm. Here 0.08 mm is the aluminum thickness, so it fits 7607.20.10. The statistical suffix is probably 7607.20.1000, though 7607.20.5000 (the "Other" line) is the alternative. Since the foil is within the thickness limit, I choose 7607.20.1000.

However, the protective film and topcoat might also shift the classification toward plastics (3921). The aluminum layer gives the essential character, though, so heading 7607 is the better fit.

{"hts_code": "7607.20.1000", "reason": "The multilayer laminate gets its essential character from the 0.08 mm aluminum foil backed with PET film, so it is classified as backed aluminum foil not over 0.15 mm thick (excluding backing) under heading 7607."}
